newsitem.title: UK: Britain presses Saudis about nurses' jail ordeal.
newsitem.headline: Britain presses Saudis about nurses' jail ordeal.

text.p: Britain said on Friday it was concerned about the "primeval" conditions in which two British nurses charged with murder in Saudi Arabia were being held.

A spokesman for the Foreign Office said Britain had contacted the Saudi authorities and pressed them to move Lucille McLauchlan and Deborah Parry, who are on trial for the alleged murder of their Australian colleague Yvonne Gilford, 55, last December.
Gilford was found stabbed 13 times, bludgeoned and suffocated in her room at the King Fhad military medical complex in the eastern oil city of Dhahran.
So far the Saudis have not responded to the British request and McLauchlan, 31, and Parry, 38, are still being held in prison in Dammam, near Dhahran.

"There have been press reports describing the prison conditions where they are being held as 'primeval' and obviously we are concerned about these conditions and pressing the Saudi authorities to move the nurses to better accommodation," the spokesman said.
"We will continue to seek an improvement in the conditions of detention. We are also pursing the issue with the nurses' lawyer and keeping the family in the picture as well," he added.
The nurses' Saudi lawyer, Salah al-Hejailan, said the families of the two women visited them in prison on Thursday before their first court appearance in three weeks.
He said the families were in good spirits but were distressed that Gilford's brother had said capital punishment was appropriate in the case.
Under Islamic sharia law the victim's family can demand the death penalty.
The nurses, who have professed their innocence, have withdrawn what they said were forced confessions.

Hejailan said the families hoped to be allowed to attend the next court hearing on Sunday and would remain in the kingdom until Wednesday. He said if the court, which adjourned on July 7 for deliberation, nullifed the confessions the case could be shelved or dismissed.
Britain's Foreign Office said their consul in Saudi Arabia had visited the nurses on Tuesday and they appeared fit and well.
"But we are obviously concerned about the conditions in the prison. In the past we have succeeded in getting the nurses moved to better accommodation," he said.
